boards.title: Your First Weekend at Duquesne University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A gentle, under-21-safe first-weekend loop across the Bluff: orient yourself, settle into campus spaces, and leave room for a new connection.

cards.title: Start with a campus map
cards.subtitle: Administration Building kiosk
cards.notes: Pick up a map from the kiosk outside the Administration Building, then use it to make your first walk feel less like a maze.
cards.short_summary: A practical first stop for getting your bearings on the Bluff.
cards.evidence_claim: Duquesne says visitors can take a self-guided walk by getting a map from the kiosk outside the Administration Building.
cards.access_notes: The university directs self-guided visitors to the kiosk outside the building for a map.

cards.title: Take the Academic Walk loop
cards.subtitle: Campus pedestrian corridor
cards.notes: Walk Academic Walk at an unhurried pace and use the green space and skyline view to identify buildings you will revisit during the week.
cards.short_summary: A campus-spine stroll that connects the weekend’s stops.
cards.evidence_claim: Duquesne describes Academic Walk as a campus route with green spaces and a view of the city skyline.
cards.access_notes: Use normal campus pedestrian access and follow posted campus guidance.

cards.title: Pause at the Unico Family Pavilion
cards.subtitle: Between College Hall, the School of Music, and Academic Walk
cards.notes: Bring your map or a friend to the shaded tables at the pavilion for a short reset before choosing the next stop.
cards.short_summary: A named outdoor seating stop beside Academic Walk.
cards.evidence_claim: Duquesne states that the Unico Family Pavilion has shaded seating and tables for students and is occasionally used as an event space.
cards.access_notes: The pavilion is on campus near Academic Walk; check posted event use before settling in.

cards.title: Find a study spot before classes begin
cards.subtitle: Gumberg Library
cards.notes: Walk through the library and note a quiet floor, group-study option, and service desk so your first study session has an easy starting point.
cards.short_summary: A five-story library stop for planning the academic week.
cards.evidence_claim: Duquesne describes Gumberg Library as having individual and collaborative study areas, private and group rooms, technology, and collections.
cards.access_notes: Confirm building hours and any room-reservation rules before planning a longer session.

cards.title: Make a quiet stop at the Grotto
cards.subtitle: Behind the Administration Building
cards.notes: Take a few minutes at the Grotto for quiet reflection, then return to the main paths rather than cutting through unfamiliar areas.
cards.short_summary: A named campus space for a calm pause.
cards.evidence_claim: Duquesne says the Lourdes Grotto behind the Administration Building has been a campus space for private prayer and contemplation since 1956.
cards.access_notes: Located behind the Administration Building; treat the space respectfully and follow any posted guidance.

cards.title: Step into the Chapel of the Holy Spirit
cards.subtitle: Adjacent to Old Main
cards.notes: If a quiet indoor break sounds right, visit the chapel for a few minutes of reflection and check the ministry page for worship details.
cards.short_summary: An all-hours chapel stop adjacent to Old Main.
cards.evidence_claim: Duquesne says the Chapel of the Holy Spirit is open all hours and encourages students to visit for personal, quiet prayer.
cards.access_notes: The university states the Chapel is open all hours; respect services and the reflective purpose of the space.

cards.title: Try a low-key NiteSpot hangout
cards.subtitle: First floor, Duquesne Union
cards.notes: Meet a hallmate in the NiteSpot for billiards, table tennis, shuffleboard, or a movie-room break; check Campus Link for that week’s programs.
cards.short_summary: A late-evening, alcohol-free recreation stop in the Union.
cards.evidence_claim: Duquesne lists billiards, table tennis, shuffleboard, and a TV/movie room at the first-floor Union NiteSpot.
cards.access_notes: Duquesne says the NiteSpot is open until midnight and until 1 a.m. on weekends; verify changes through Campus Link.

cards.title: Move a little at the Power Center
cards.subtitle: Campus recreation and fitness facility
cards.notes: Choose a low-pressure introduction: walk the indoor track, ask about group fitness, or learn where intramural and club-sport information is posted.
cards.short_summary: A recreation stop with fitness, track, and class options.
cards.evidence_claim: Duquesne describes the Power Center as an 80,000-square-foot recreation and fitness facility with an indoor track, intramurals, club sports, and group fitness classes.
cards.access_notes: The official page lists Saturday hours of 9 a.m.–2 p.m.; facility use may require university eligibility or ID access.

cards.title: See Rooney Field from Academic Walk
cards.subtitle: Central campus field beside Academic Walk
cards.notes: Follow Academic Walk to Rooney Field and take in the field’s campus setting; save any game plans for a schedule you have independently confirmed.
cards.short_summary: An on-campus athletic landmark beside the pedestrian corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: Duquesne identifies Rooney Field as the home field for its football, soccer, and women’s lacrosse teams and notes its location by Academic Walk.
cards.access_notes: View from public campus paths; attend only events for which entry and schedule have been confirmed.

cards.title: Locate the UPMC Cooper Fieldhouse
cards.subtitle: Duquesne athletics venue
cards.notes: Find the Fieldhouse on your campus loop so you know where to look for future athletic events; check official athletics information before attending.
cards.short_summary: A named on-campus home court and athletic training venue.
cards.evidence_claim: Duquesne states that UPMC Cooper Fieldhouse is home court for its men’s and women’s basketball teams and supports other student-athlete training.
cards.access_notes: Access to games, practices, and interior areas depends on the event or facility rules; confirm before entering.
